item.content:encoded: After nine days trapped in a hydropower tunnel and a week of hospital care following his [USN:L4N45317T TEXT:"dramatic rescue"], Sanjay Sah, a rare survivor of last month's devastating glacier collapse in Nepal, finally returned to his village and family on Sunday. It was a homecoming marked by relief and joy but also grief. "I was trapped in the tunnel ... I felt trapped in the hospital room too. I finally feel free here in my village," Sah, 30, said after arriving in Tilathi Koiladi, near the border with India. At least 1,386 people have died and 5,130 are still missing across Nepal weeks after a Himalayan glacier collapsed near the Chinese border, unleashing a wall of mud and water that crashed through mountain valleys destroying everything in its path. Around 900 power station workers remain missing. Sah, a mechanical foreman at the Upper Trishuli 3A Hydropower Station, was one of just three [USN:L6N44W0G4 TEXT:"pulled from debris-buried tunnels"] extending deep under the mountains. He survived in the darkness, drinking flood water and seepage from the mountain rock until rescue workers finally reached him. Sah left the hospital in the capital Kathmandu on Friday and the next day boarded a bus for an overnight journey home. A TEARFUL HOMECOMING TO A VILLAGE STILL IN MOURNING Around 60 people, mostly women, awaited his arrival in Tilathi Koiladi on Sunday. Family members, including his parents, uncle, wife and daughter, performed a traditional welcome ceremony, washing his feet as part of a cleansing ritual. After his mother dabbed a pink vermilion tika on his forehead, Sah bowed. They embraced and then broke down in tears. "My son!" his mother cried, holding him tightly and kissing him on the cheek. Women who had gathered to witness the reunion used their colourful saris to wipe the tears from their eyes. Many in Tilathi Koiladi are still awaiting word of the fate of family members who had been working at hydropower stations hit by the flooding. "There are more people from my village still missing after the flood," Sah told Reuters. One family, he said, phoned him while he was still in the hospital to ask if he had seen or heard from a missing relative who had been working at a different power station. He had to tell them he had not. At home among family, Sah said he is ready to put his ordeal behind him. "I will stay in my village for some time now. I want to meet all my people," he said. "But if I am called back to duty, I will go."

item.title: Trump dice que EEUU podría permanecer en Irán y quedarse con el petróleo, como en acuerdo con Venezuela
item.description: El presidente Donald Trump sugirió el domingo que Estados Unidos podría permanecer en Irán y "quedarse con el petróleo", estableciendo un paralelismo con la iniciativa estadounidense de hacerse con el control de una quinta parte de las enormes reservas petroleras de Venezuela.
item.dc:creator: Bo Erickson, Conor Humphries
item.content:encoded: El presidente Donald Trump sugirió el domingo que Estados Unidos podría permanecer en Irán y "quedarse con el petróleo", estableciendo un paralelismo con la iniciativa estadounidense de hacerse con el control de una quinta parte de las enormes reservas petroleras de Venezuela. Durante un viaje a Irlanda para asistir a reuniones y ver un torneo de golf, reiteró que seguía esperando que la guerra con Irán termine este año, posiblemente justo después de las elecciones legislativas de mitad de mandato que se celebrarán en Estados Unidos en noviembre. En declaraciones realizadas durante el campeonato de golf Irish Open, Trump añadió que el precio de la gasolina "caería en picado" una vez que termine la guerra con Irán. La agitación en Oriente Medio ha sacudido los mercados petroleros, y los operadores de crudo prevén que los precios vuelvan a subir el lunes tras un ataque contra un oleoducto saudí. Trump dijo que solo aceptaría el "acuerdo adecuado" y que no firmaría uno que "no valiera la pena", añadiendo que Irán estaba "pidiendo constantemente" negociaciones de paz —una afirmación que Teherán ha desmentido en el pasado—. Pero el presidente también planteó otra opción: seguir manteniendo el diálogo con Irán. Estableció un paralelismo con el acuerdo de Estados Unidos en Venezuela, anunciado en agosto. "Al final nos retiraremos (de Irán), a menos que decidamos quedarnos y quedarnos con el petróleo, como en Venezuela", dijo Trump, añadiendo que los ingresos de Estados Unidos procedentes de Venezuela han "pagado la guerra muchas veces".

item.title: Trump le dice al presidente ucraniano Zelenski que deje de atacar el diésel ruso
item.description: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, pidió el domingo al presidente ucraniano, Volodímir Zelenski, que deje de atacar las infraestructuras rusas relacionadas con el diésel.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, pidió el domingo al presidente ucraniano, Volodímir Zelenski, que deje de atacar las infraestructuras rusas relacionadas con el diésel. "Hemos hablado con el señor Zelenski sobre ello. Hay muchos otros objetivos. No ataque el combustible diésel", dijo Trump a periodistas durante una visita a Irlanda. "Hay que dejar de atacar el combustible diésel en Rusia", añadió.

item.title: Trump dice que "fuerzas muy negativas" están generando preocupaciones exageradas sobre la IA
item.description: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, comparó el domingo a los detractores de la inteligencia artificial con "fuerzas muy negativas" que plantean escenarios que no se producirán, y dijo que quería asegurarse de que Estados Unidos siga siendo líder del sector.
item.dc:creator: Bo Erickson, Padraic Halpin
item.content:encoded: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, comparó el domingo a los detractores de la inteligencia artificial con "fuerzas muy negativas" que plantean escenarios que no se producirán, y dijo que quería asegurarse de que Estados Unidos siga siendo líder del sector. "Lideramos a China en IA. Somos el país más avanzado del mundo y, francamente, quiero que siga siendo así, porque quien gane en IA, gana", dijo Trump a periodistas en su campo de golf de Irlanda, cuando se le preguntó si el sector de la IA debería ralentizarse o estar más regulado. "Podríamos establecer medidas de protección. Podemos hacer esto y aquello. Pero creo que hay muchas fuerzas muy negativas que están sacando el tema a colación cuando no deberían hacerlo, y están planteando cosas que no van a suceder". Trump se ha resistido a avivar las preocupaciones sobre la IA. El debate público sobre la IA ha ganado fuerza en Estados Unidos después de que dos investigadores de Anthropic advirtieron que esta tecnología, que avanza a pasos agigantados, podría provocar la extinción de la raza humana en un futuro no muy lejano. En su segundo mandato, el Gobierno de Trump ha dado un gran apoyo a las empresas de IA. Estos líderes del sector de la IA y otras empresas tecnológicas también han respaldado las iniciativas de Trump. Los ejecutivos del sector de la IA han invertido grandes sumas de dinero en la campaña para las elecciones legislativas de mitad de mandato, que se celebrarán el 3 de noviembre y determinarán quién controlará el Congreso. El super PAC de Elon Musk, director ejecutivo de SpaceX, "America PAC", ya ha gastado millones en apoyar a candidatos republicanos y se espera que desempeñe un papel fundamental en los esfuerzos por fomentar la participación electoral este otoño boreal. El Pentágono advirtió este año de los riesgos que plantea el modelo de Anthropic. Tras las advertencias de los investigadores, algunos directores generales del sector de la IA están presionando para que se ralentice el avance de los modelos. El sábado, el director ejecutivo de Anthropic, Dario Amodei, esbozó un marco de tres pasos destinado a moderar el ritmo de desarrollo y disponer de más tiempo para gestionar sus riesgos. La propuesta recibió inmediatamente el respaldo de varios otros ejecutivos de importantes empresas de IA, entre ellos Musk y el director ejecutivo de OpenAI, Sam Altman. En una entrevista emitida el domingo en el programa "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" de CBS, Amodei dijo que la competencia entre las empresas de IA estadounidenses y chinas era el "dilema más difícil" a la hora de intentar establecer un "límite de velocidad" en el ritmo de desarrollo de la IA. "No debemos engañarnos, porque los incentivos para tomar la delantera y la ventaja militar que ello supone son tan grandes que la capacidad de comprobar que la otra parte no está haciendo trampa tiene que ser a toda prueba", afirmó. "Así que creo que eso va a llevar años y, sinceramente, no sé si será posible". Jacob Coxon, uno de los investigadores de Anthropic que renunció y posteriormente lanzó estas advertencias, instó a Estados Unidos a colaborar con otros países para garantizar un ritmo adecuado. "Creo que necesitamos coordinación internacional; de lo contrario, corremos el riesgo de enzarzarnos en la misma carrera con China, lo que podría resultar igualmente peligroso", dijo Coxon en el programa "Meet the Press" de NBC.

item.title: Reds out to end miserable road trip with win against Brewers
item.description: The Cincinnati Reds will hope to end what's been a brutal road trip on a high note Sunday when they face the Milwaukee Brewers for the final time this season.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Cincinnati Reds will hope to end what's been a brutal road trip on a high note Sunday when they face the Milwaukee Brewers for the final time this season. Manager Terry Francona's team is 0-5 against the Los Angeles Dodgers and Brewers so far on their six-game road trip and is a loss away from being swept on a multi-stop trip for the second time this season. Cincinnati (69-79) started May losing three at Pittsburgh and then four at the Chicago Cubs, a stretch that derailed a 20-11 start to this season. Reds ace Chase Burns (15-3, 2.73 ERA) will start Sunday's game, but the right-hander, 23, will be on a short leash as he's thrown 148 1/3 innings already in his first full big-league season. He owns a win this season against the Brewers (93-56), having allowed two runs on four hits and two walks and struck out four in the 7-2 Reds road victory over Milwaukee ace Jacob Misiorowski on July 2. Factoring in a relief appearance last season, Burns is 1-0 with a 2.35 ERA in 7 2/3 innings with eight strikeouts. Even if the Reds salvage Sunday's finale, it will not atone for a historically bad stretch for the team's pitchers. After a 14-1 loss to the Dodgers on Wednesday, the Reds were blown out 20-0 by Milwaukee on Friday and lost 13-9 Saturday. According to Stathead, the 47 runs are the most any team has given up over a three-game span this season and are the most the Reds have yielded since 1901. They gave up a record 51 from Sept. 22-24 of that season and 50 from Sept. 23-25. Dating back to 1898, only those instances from nearly 125 years ago top what the team has allowed in its past three games. It's put Francona in a tough position as he tries to finish out the final two weeks of the season. "Just making sure they understand that we don't want to hurt anybody," Francona said when asked about handling the staff. "We got innings to fill, and we care about them. And they're OK." Robert Gasser (4-5, 4.43) is the scheduled starter for the Brewers. The left-hander, 27, has faced the Reds twice as a starter, going 0-1 with a 3.24 ERA in 8 1/3 innings. He threw 5 2/3 innings in Cincinnati on June 29, giving up three runs in the Brewers' 5-3 win. Offensively for Milwaukee, Garrett Mitchell is 7-for-10 in the first two games of the series with two home runs and eight RBIs. The two four-RBI performances are one off his season-high, which he achieved on April 4 in a 5-2 win at Kansas City. Not all, though, has gone right for Milwaukee of late. On Saturday, manager Pat Murphy brought starter Kyle Harrison to pitch in relief for the first time this season. Harrison, who last pitched last Sunday in Cincinnati, had given up 16 runs (14 earned) in his previous three starts, a total of 12 1/3 innings. Coming in to start the eighth up 13-5, Harrison did not record an out as all four Reds batters he faced got a hit and scored. On Aug. 18, after he was the winning pitcher in Milwaukee's 22-0 romp over the Seattle Mariners, Harrison had a 2.84 ERA and a 10-3 record. Since then, he is 0-1 with a 12.41 ERA in 12 1/3 innings, raising his season ERA to 3.98. Murphy, according to the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel, said after the win that Harrison may be dealing with a confidence issue that's starting to affect him physically. "We'll get this straight," he said. "This will happen. We're going through a rough patch." --Field Level Media

item.title: Antes de reunión de la Fed, Trump dice que EEUU debería tener tasa más baja del mundo
item.description: El presidente Donald Trump dijo el domingo que ningún país debería tener tasas de interés más bajas que Estados Unidos, a pocos días de la próxima reunión de política monetaria de la Reserva Federal.
item.dc:creator: Bo Erickson, Padraic Halpin, Conor Humphries
item.content:encoded: El presidente Donald Trump dijo el domingo que ningún país debería tener tasas de interés más bajas que Estados Unidos, a pocos días de la próxima reunión de política monetaria de la Reserva Federal. En declaraciones a periodistas durante el torneo de golf Irish Open, Trump dijo que no sabía si los responsables a cargo de la política monetaria de la Fed subirían las tasas de interés en su reunión de esta semana. No obstante, defendió que Estados Unidos "debería tener la tasa de interés más baja del mundo", independientemente de lo que indiquen los datos de la Reserva Federal sobre la inflación y la economía. La reunión de la Fed tendrá lugar menos de una semana después de que un indicador clave de la inflación subyacente, el Índice de Precios al Consumidor del Departamento de Trabajo, registró el viernes su mayor subida en cuatro meses. Esto reforzó las expectativas de que el banco central estadounidense subirá las tasas. Los gobernadores del banco central se reúnen apenas unas semanas antes de las elecciones legislativas de mitad de mandato, que determinarán si los republicanos conservan sus escasas mayorías en ambas cámaras del Congreso de Estados Unidos. Una subida de las tasas podría agravar las preocupaciones de los votantes sobre la asequibilidad, según recientes encuestas de Reuters/Ipsos. Los índices de aprobación de Trump han caído a medida que la inflación se ha mantenido alta. El republicano ha argumentado que los niveles de las tasas de interés de la Fed han favorecido a otros países a costa de Estados Unidos. "Sé más de fórmulas que nadie y, con el mejor crédito del mundo, hacemos ricos a otros países", dijo Trump el domingo. El presidente, que ha criticado con frecuencia al expresidente de la Fed, Jay Powell, se ha mostrado más favorable al liderazgo de la Fed desde que su propio candidato a la presidencia, Kevin Warsh, asumió el cargo a principios de este año. Sin embargo, Trump ha dejado más claras sus exigencias recientemente. "BAJEN LAS TASAS O DEJARÉ DE COMERCIAR CON LOS PAÍSES CON LOS QUE TENEMOS DÉFICIT", publicó Trump en las redes sociales hace dos semanas. Trump "defenderá la independencia de Kevin Warsh por encima de todo", independientemente de lo que haga la Fed con las tasas de interés, dijo el director del Consejo Económico Nacional, Kevin Hassett, en el programa "Fox News Sunday". No obstante, Hassett también subrayó las preferencias del propio Trump, afirmando que "si se trata de una subida de tasas… estoy seguro de que no le va a hacer mucha gracia".

item.title: Emmanuel Rodriguez, Twins eye encore vs. Guardians
item.description: Forgive Emmanuel Rodriguez if he still appears to be floating on air Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Forgive Emmanuel Rodriguez if he still appears to be floating on air Sunday. The Minnesota Twins outfielder might still be trying to come to grips with his dream debut, in which he homered in his first at-bat in the big leagues. His blast sparked a four-run third inning, which proved to be enough for a 4-3 win over the Cleveland Guardians on Saturday. Now comes a high-stakes rubber match as the regular season nears its end. Cleveland (75-74) will try to win the series when it takes on Minnesota (70-78) on Sunday afternoon in Minneapolis. The Guardians slipped 1 1/2 games behind the Chicago White Sox for first place in the American League Central after the Guardians' loss on Saturday, but they still have time to try to rally for the division title. Cleveland, which currently holds the third and final AL wild-card spot, will host Chicago in a crucial three-game series starting Monday night. Meanwhile, the Twins face long odds in their quest for a wild-card playoff berth, and they know the only way to achieve their goal is by putting together a string of wins. Rodriguez will try to do his part. After he was promoted from Triple-A Saint Paul on Saturday, he blasted a 420-foot home run over the wall in center field. "I'm still going through that moment where nothing feels real yet," Rodriguez said. "But I know once I go and have a good time with my family and am able to reflect on it, that's when it's going to feel more real. Right now, I'm still riding that high of all the emotions." Cleveland will try to subdue the Twins' excitement in the series finale. Right-hander Tanner Bibee (5-15, 4.22 ERA) is slated to start. Bibee will try to find his footing after enduring tough outings in his past two starts. He did not get out of the fifth inning either time, including in his most recent start, when he allowed five runs on six hits in 4 1/3 innings in his team's 9-5 win over the Baltimore Orioles on Tuesday. This will be Bibee's 12th career start against the Twins. He is 3-0 with a 2.84 ERA in his first 11 meetings and has walked 16 and struck out 69 in 63 1/3 innings. Minnesota likely will counter with right-hander Joe Ryan (6-9, 3.68 ERA), who is in line to make his 25th start. He also will look to bounce back from a bumpy stretch in which he has lost his past four starts. In his most recent outing, Ryan allowed three runs (two earned) on three hits in four innings in a 5-4 defeat to the Detroit Tigers on Monday. He walked one and struck out seven. Ryan is no stranger to facing Cleveland. He is 3-6 with a 3.59 ERA in 14 career games (13 starts) against the franchise. Guardians manager Stephen Vogt doesn't think his players need to change their approach after Saturday's loss. Despite falling short, the team had a good showing at the plate, he said. "I thought we had good at-bats," Vogt said. "We hit a lot of balls hard, right at people. We got traffic. ... We just weren't able to score enough runs." Twins shortstop Kaelen Culpepper's status is uncertain for Sunday's game. He left after being hit by a pitch and sustaining a shoulder contusion on Saturday, and the team described him as day to day. --Field Level Media

item.title: Kosovo parliament re-elects Albin Kurti as prime minister, political crisis persists
item.description: Kosovo's parliament re-elected Albin Kurti as prime minister on Sunday after his party came first in June elections, but a failure to elect a president could send the country into another snap election.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Kosovo's parliament re-elected Albin Kurti as prime minister on Sunday after his party came first in June elections, but a failure to elect a president could send the country into another snap election. Kurti was elected with 62 votes in the 120-seat parliament. "This mandate is about strongly restoring security and prosperity for citizens," Kurti said before the vote. "Repeated elections have only interrupted the same government from governing." In late August, Kurti reached a deal with the opposition Democratic League of Kosovo (LDK), which has 18 MPs, to back law professor Bekim Sejdiu as the new president. A day later, six LDK lawmakers said they would not respect their leader's decision. It remains unclear when the presidential vote will take place. If parliament fails to elect a new president, Kosovo would have to hold another snap election, the fourth in only two years. Kosovo, one of Europe's poorest countries, aims to join the European Union but Brussels has repeatedly said the country needs stable institutions capable of delivering reforms required for membership. Political instability has delayed reforms and slowed access to EU funding. Two-thirds of votes are needed to elect the president, who largely has a ceremonial role. Two opposition parties, the Democratic Party of Kosovo (PDK) and the Alliance, boycotted the session and said they would ask the Constitutional Court whether the law was violated when parliament was constituted. LDK also did not take part in the voting of the new government.

item.title: Interrupción de oleoducto saudí amenaza con provocar pérdida de 4% del suministro mundial de crudo
item.description: Arabia Saudita se quedará sin reservas de petróleo para la exportación si no reanuda en los próximos días el funcionamiento de su principal oleoducto hacia el mar Rojo, lo que provocaría una pérdida de hasta el 4% del suministro mundial, señalaron compradores y operadores de petróleo saudíes.
item.dc:creator: Alex Lawler, Dmitry Zhdannikov
item.content:encoded: Arabia Saudita se quedará sin reservas de petróleo para la exportación si no reanuda en los próximos días el funcionamiento de su principal oleoducto hacia el mar Rojo, lo que provocaría una pérdida de hasta el 4% del suministro mundial, señalaron compradores y operadores de petróleo saudíes. Una nueva disminución de los flujos saudíes agravará la escasez de suministro mundial, que ya ha empujado los precios mundiales del combustible a máximos históricos, ha impulsado la inflación en todo el mundo y ha llevado los rendimientos de los bonos estadounidenses a los niveles más altos desde la crisis financiera de 2008. Desde que los ataques con drones obligaron a Arabia Saudita a cerrar el viernes su enorme oleoducto este-oeste, Riad no ha facilitado detalles completos sobre la magnitud de los daños ni sobre cuánto tiempo permanecerá fuera de servicio el trazado. Las fuentes consultadas por Reuters ofrecieron estimaciones dispares: una de ellas dijo que la reparación de los daños podría llevar entre cinco y seis semanas, mientras que otra señaló que podría solucionarse antes y que el bombeo podría reanudarse parcialmente mientras se llevan a cabo las reparaciones. La oficina de prensa del Gobierno de Arabia Saudita y el Ministerio de Energía no respondieron de inmediato a las solicitudes de comentarios. Durante los últimos seis meses, el oleoducto que atraviesa el desierto de la Península Arábiga ha evitado que Arabia Saudita sufra de lleno el impacto del cierre del estrecho de Ormuz durante la guerra, que ha paralizado las exportaciones de sus vecinos. El mayor exportador del mundo ha utilizado el oleoducto para desviar alrededor de 4 millones de barriles al día —aproximadamente el 4% del suministro mundial— hacia el puerto de Yanbu, en el mar Rojo. Sin embargo, con el oleoducto fuera de servicio, Yanbu cuenta ahora con reservas suficientes para mantener las exportaciones durante solo entre cinco y siete días, según tres fuentes del sector familiarizadas con las exportaciones saudíes. Arabia Saudita también dispone de reservas para abastecer a sus clientes durante varios días desde los puertos egipcios de Ain Sukhna, en el mar Rojo, y Sidi Kerir, en el Mediterráneo, según una cuarta fuente. La capacidad de almacenamiento de Yanbu ronda los 35 millones de barriles, según estimaciones del sector, mientras que Ain Sukhna y Sidi Kerir pueden almacenar 18 y 20 millones de barriles, respectivamente. Las reservas no están llenas y, en última instancia, se agotarán si el oleoducto este-oeste no reanuda sus operaciones, afirmaron las cuatro fuentes. El suministro de petróleo saudí ya ha caído en agosto a su nivel más bajo en más de tres décadas debido a la reducción de los flujos a través de Ormuz y el mar Rojo, informó el viernes la Agencia Internacional de la Energía. El suministro mundial de petróleo descenderá este año en 5,7 millones de barriles diarios, lo que supone alrededor del 6%, según la AIE, que coordina las políticas energéticas occidentales. Además del ataque al oleoducto, los combatientes hutíes de Yemen, que han amenazado los envíos de petróleo saudí, se hicieron el viernes con el control de una isla situada en la desembocadura del mar Rojo. Oriente Medio suministraba alrededor de 22 millones de barriles diarios de petróleo antes de la guerra. Según fuentes del sector, los flujos a través del estrecho de Ormuz se han reducido a tan solo entre 6 y 9 millones de barriles diarios. Arabia Saudita comunicó a la OPEP la semana pasada que su producción de petróleo había caído hasta apenas 6,2 millones de barriles diarios en agosto, frente a los 10,9 millones de barriles diarios registrados en febrero, antes del inicio de la guerra.

item.title: White Sox take on Cardinals, look to head into crucial division series on a winning streak
item.description: After coming up with perhaps the biggest hit of the year for the Chicago White Sox, veteran Randal Grichuk said his team could move beyond a September slump and win the American League Central title.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: After coming up with perhaps the biggest hit of the year for the Chicago White Sox, veteran Randal Grichuk said his team could move beyond a September slump and win the American League Central title. Grichuk's go-ahead, two-run home run with the visiting White Sox down to their last strike in the ninth inning Saturday helped them stop a four-game losing streak, add to their division lead, and put them in position to win the three-game series against the St. Louis Cardinals on Sunday afternoon. The White Sox (76-72) had lost nine of their past 12 games, and their 5 1/2-game division lead in mid-August had shrunk to a half-game -- until Grichuk's heroics and a loss by the second-place Cleveland Guardians on Saturday. The White Sox will head to Cleveland on Monday for a crucial three-game series that will help to decide the division winner. But for now, Chicago can exhale briefly with 14 games to go in the regular season after their comeback victory on Saturday. "Huge," Grichuk said. "Obviously it's getting late in the year and everything matters, so hopefully now we can keep playing our game and get to a lot better place." The White Sox are in a much better place than in the past three seasons, all of which ended with at least 100 losses, including a record 121 two years ago. Grichuk, who just turned 35 having played parts of 13 seasons in the majors, has been a key addition after signing as a free agent in early May. He's batting .286 with a .568 slugging percentage, fueled by 13 homers and 23 doubles in 238 plate appearances overall. The New York Yankees cut Grichuk a month into the season after signing him late in spring training. He got off to a slow start, batting just .194, and the Yankees' move proved to be fortuitous for the White Sox. Teammates praise Grichuk for not only fitting in but also leading the way. "Never count him out," catcher Kyle Teel said. "A leader of this team. He's always getting the job done." Grichuk's home run against Cardinals closer Riley O'Brien came on a 1-2 pitch -- a sinker on the outer half that wasn't at top velocity and caught too much of the plate. Cardinals manager Oliver Marmol implied that a breaking ball in the dirt would have been a better approach. "There's different ways of attacking that one," he said. Grichuk said he suspected a wipeout sweeper but also was prepared for what he got. He'll take it. So will the White Sox. "It was something that we really needed," Grichuk said. The Cardinals (73-76) are close to being eliminated from the National League wild-card race as they start Sunday 7 1/2 games out of the final spot. But they are excited by the recent contributions of young players such as rookie catcher Leo Bernal, whose tie-breaking homer in the eighth against Grant Taylor put them in position to win on Saturday. "That would have been a cool moment," Marmol said. "I wish we would have been able to keep the lead and shake hands and get the hell out of here." Bernal has three homers and is hitting .311 in 11 games since making his major league debut. Right-hander Michael McGreevy (6-9, 3.92 ERA) will start for the Cardinals on Sunday. He has a 6.26 ERA in nine starts since late July and is 1-2 in that span. McGreevy has faced the White Sox once in his career, on June 19, 2025, when he allowed a run, three hits and a walk to go with five strikeouts over five innings. He did not get a decision in the 8-6, 10-inning win. The White Sox haven't yet named a starting pitcher for Sunday's game, but right-hander Sean Burke (8-7, 3.58 ERA) was due to pitch. The White Sox appear to be sorting out their rotation heading into the series vs. the Guardians. --Field Level Media

item.title: Nuevo reporte de ataque a buque en Ormuz aviva temores de amenazas al suministro de crudo
item.description: Los servicios de seguimiento marítimo recibieron el domingo nuevos informes de un ataque a un buque en el estrecho de Ormuz, lo que agravó la preocupación por las amenazas relacionadas con Irán para el suministro energético mundial, tras el cierre por parte de Arabia Saudita de un oleoducto de vital importancia.
item.dc:creator: Mohammed Ghobari, Menna Alaaeldin
item.content:encoded: Los servicios de seguimiento marítimo recibieron el domingo nuevos informes de un ataque a un buque en el estrecho de Ormuz, lo que agravó la preocupación por las amenazas relacionadas con Irán para el suministro energético mundial, tras el cierre por parte de Arabia Saudita de un oleoducto de vital importancia. La agencia UKMTO, afiliada a la Armada británica, dijo que recibió un informe sobre un proyectil que impactó en un buque mientras este atravesaba el estrecho. La tripulación fue evacuada por las autoridades locales tras declararse un incendio a raíz del ataque, informó la agencia el domingo. El informe de la UKMTO se produjo un día después de que Arabia Saudita anunció el cierre temporal de su oleoducto Este-Oeste como medida de precaución, tras un ataque con drones que, según Bagdad y Riad, se había originado en Irak, donde operan milicias respaldadas por Irán. Los continuos ataques en la guerra de Oriente Medio podrían hacer que los precios de la energía suban aún más tras una semana en la que el precio del crudo Brent volvió a superar los 100 dólares por barril. El oleoducto Este-Oeste, de 1.200 km (745 millas) de longitud, que atraviesa la Península Arábiga, ha servido como principal vía de salida para los suministros mundiales de petróleo de Oriente Medio durante los últimos seis meses, mientras el estrecho de Ormuz ha permanecido prácticamente cerrado por la guerra. Ha transportado entre 4 y 5 millones de barriles al día, lo que supone entre el 4% y el 5% del suministro mundial, lo que ha evitado a Arabia Saudita sufrir de lleno las perturbaciones que han paralizado a otros exportadores de petróleo y gas del Golfo. Nadie reivindicó de inmediato la autoría de los ataques contra el oleoducto. Las imágenes de satélite mostraban humo negro elevándose desde una zona del oleoducto al sur de Medina. El ataque provocó algunos heridos y daños que se estaban evaluando, informó el Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores saudí, sin detallar el impacto en las exportaciones. El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, de visita en Irlanda para asistir a un torneo de golf en uno de sus complejos turísticos, dijo que probablemente Irán era el responsable. El sábado, la Defensa Civil saudí dijo en un comunicado que un proyectil disparado por los hutíes había herido a dos personas en la región de Jazan y dañado varios edificios, incluida una mezquita. Los medios estatales iraníes informaron que un buque mercante iraní fue alcanzado frente a su costa sur a primera hora del domingo, lo que causó la muerte de una persona y dejó heridas a otras tres, sin dar más detalles. La cadena de televisión Al Masirah, controlada por los hutíes, dijo el domingo que Arabia Saudita realizó tres ataques aéreos sobre la zona de al-Rubaie, en la provincia de Taiz, al suroeste de Yemen. No hubo confirmación oficial por parte de Arabia Saudita. El sábado, los hutíes dijeron que se habían producido 129 ataques aéreos saudíes en las últimas 48 horas. LÍDER SAUDÍ SOLICITA AYUDA MILITAR A EEUU Los precios del petróleo se dispararon durante la semana pasada y el precio al por menor del diésel en Estados Unidos superó el récord de 6 dólares por galón, al tiempo que tanto Estados Unidos como Irán atacaban petroleros y los hutíes en Yemen avanzaban rápidamente a lo largo del mar Rojo, lo que podría dar a Teherán influencia sobre los dos principales corredores de transporte de petróleo de la región. Washington se enfrenta ahora al dilema de si ayudar a los saudíes a combatir a los hutíes, con el riesgo de que la guerra se extienda aún más. El gobernante de facto de Arabia Saudita, el príncipe heredero Mohammed bin Salman, llamó por teléfono a Trump el jueves y le pidió ayuda militar estadounidense para combatir a los hutíes, informaron tres fuentes a Reuters. Dijeron que se le comunicó al príncipe que Washington no intervendría directamente por el momento, pero que prestaría ayuda en materia de inteligencia. Trump confirmó el sábado que había hablado con el príncipe heredero y señaló que los hutíes también habían llamado a su administración para pedir a Washington que no se involucrara directamente en el conflicto. Cuatro fuentes del Gobierno yemení informaron a Reuters que los hutíes se habían apoderado el viernes de la estratégica isla de Perim, situada en medio del estrecho de Bab el-Mandeb —la "Puerta de las Lágrimas", en la entrada sur del mar Rojo—. Los hutíes llevan atacando buques saudíes en la zona desde que declararon un bloqueo en julio y han estado atacando otras instalaciones petroleras del país. UN FUNCIONARIO IRANÍ MINIMIZA LA REUNIÓN EN OMÁN No se han celebrado conversaciones entre Estados Unidos e Irán para poner fin al conflicto desde el acuerdo de junio, que se vino abajo en cuestión de semanas. En una publicación en X el sábado, Ebrahim Azizi, presidente de la comisión de seguridad nacional del Parlamento iraní, dijo: "Mientras la parte estadounidense no acepte todas las condiciones de Irán, el diálogo y la negociación no sirven de nada". El Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores de Teherán anunció el viernes que Irán asistiría el lunes a una reunión con los Estados árabes del Golfo en Omán, en la que se debatiría el futuro del estrecho de Ormuz. Sin embargo, un alto funcionario iraní, que habló con Reuters el sábado bajo condición de anonimato, restó importancia a las posibilidades de un avance significativo, señalando que la reunión, convocada por iniciativa de Omán, tenía por objeto debatir cuestiones como la del estrecho, pero no se esperaba que diera lugar a la firma de un acuerdo. En la reunión del lunes se presentará un acuerdo sobre las rutas a través del estrecho entre Irán y Omán, pero el estrecho no se reabrirá a menos que se cumplan las siete condiciones que Irán ha transmitido a Estados Unidos, dijo una fuente a la agencia de noticias Tasnim, sin dar más detalles. Irán quiere que se reconozca su control sobre el estrecho de Ormuz, lo que le permitiría cobrar tasas a los barcos que lo utilicen, algo que Washington rechaza. Omán, que controla la orilla opuesta del estrecho, dice que está negociando con el consentimiento de otros Estados de la región. Antes de que comenzara la guerra, los buques disfrutaban de un paso libre y sin restricciones por el estrecho.

item.title: Russian athletes appeal for end to World Athletics ban
item.description: Russian athletes have appealed to international sporting and human rights bodies to help end World Athletics' ban on Russian competitors, arguing that more than four years of exclusion has deprived a generation of athletes of their careers.
item.dc:creator: Lori Ewing, Soheil Afdjei
item.content:encoded: Russian athletes have appealed to international sporting and human rights bodies to help end World Athletics' ban on Russian competitors, arguing that more than four years of exclusion has deprived a generation of athletes of their careers. In an open letter dated September 10, seen by Reuters and addressed to the International Olympic Committee (IOC) Athletes' Commission, the IOC Advisory Committee on Human Rights and the U.N. High Commissioner for Human Rights, the athletes said the continued ban was having a devastating impact. "For us, this is not an abstract legal or political issue. Athletics is our life," the letter said. "Four years is a long time in any life. In an athlete's life, it can be the most significant years." The [USN:L6N4350ZY TEXT:"World Athletics Council"] reaffirmed its decision to exclude Russian and Belarusian athletes from international competition on July 3, maintaining sanctions first imposed following Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Russian Athletics filed an appeal with the Court of Arbitration for Sport on July 9 challenging the decision and lodged a [USN:L8N4470N8 TEXT:"further appeal"] last month. While World Athletics have been contacted for comment, federation president [USN:L8N455033 TEXT:"Sebastian Coe"] reiterated earlier on Sunday that the governing body's position had not changed ahead of the arbitration proceedings. "This isn't about politics or passports. It's about the integrity of competition," Coe told reporters at the Ultimate Championship in Budapest. Coe said he recognised the importance of ultimately restoring full global participation in the sport. "We want a full complement of people on a global level competing in our sport, and that has to be our overall objective," he said. "Of course, it does." The Russian athletes argued that the federation's stance amounted to collective punishment and was out of step with other international sports federations, many of which have gradually reintroduced Russian and Belarusian athletes under neutral status. The [USN:L6N4390WH TEXT:"IOC"] provisionally lifted their suspension of the Russian Olympic Committee on July 8, marking a significant step towards the nation's reintegration into the Olympic fold ahead of the Los Angeles 2028 Games. "Athletics remains one of the very limited exceptions where Russian athletes continue to face a full blanket exclusion," the letter said. The athletes said they had separately asked the Court of Arbitration for Sport on July 17 for permission to participate in the appeal proceedings, but had yet to receive a response. They added the prolonged uncertainty was taking a personal toll. "A legal or institutional process can continue for years. An athlete's career cannot," they wrote.

item.title: Marquez seizes championship lead with San Marino win after Bezzecchi crash
item.description: Ducati's Marc Marquez seized the MotoGP championship lead for the first time this season after winning a chaotic San Marino Grand Prix on Sunday, where Aprilia's home favourite Marco Bezzecchi crashed out on the opening lap.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ducati's Marc Marquez seized the MotoGP championship lead for the first time this season after winning a chaotic San Marino Grand Prix on Sunday, where Aprilia's home favourite Marco Bezzecchi crashed out on the opening lap. Marquez claimed his fifth victory of the campaign to move level with Jorge Martin on 274 points but the seven-times champion tops the standings having won more races than the Aprilia rider, whose sole win this season came in France. Marquez finished ahead of his brother Alex of Gresini Racing while KTM's Pedro Acosta completed the podium. Fermin Aldeguer was fourth, pushing Martin down to fifth as five Spaniards finished in the top five. Leading the championship seemed a distant prospect earlier this season, with Marquez trailing Bezzecchi by 102 points after the Italian Grand Prix in May. "It feels unreal but I never give up. I will push until the end. This is not done, we are there in the championship fighting against very good riders, especially Martin and Bez," Marquez said. "But as we see today, we are riding at the limit and a small mistake can cost a lot of points." Marquez had overtaken Bezzecchi at turn one to [USN:L1N45403L TEXT:"win Saturday's sprint"] but the Italian went on the defensive in the race, taking the lead as the Aprilia -- sporting a special white livery at their home track -- surged ahead. BEZZECCHI CRASHES ON LAP ONE But Bezzecchi's attempt to build an early lead backfired dramatically when he lost control at turn 12, sending his bike cartwheeling across the gravel to the utter shock of the Italian fans. Marquez moved into the lead while his team mate Francesco Bagnaia also crashed at his home track to retire for the fourth time in five races, with Ducati CEO Claudio Domenicali unable to hide his disappointment as he doubled over in disbelief. Martin, starting fifth, had briefly seized control by overtaking Marquez on lap seven with a daring overtake on the inside at turn four. But the Aprilia rider's dreams of victory evaporated when Marc struck back on lap 12 with a dive into turn six, before Alex also swept past. "After Bezzecchi's mistake, I was a bit too confident and then Martin attacked me," Marquez said. "But then I regained the confidence again. I kept the pace and I'm happy because 37 points here means a lot." Aprilia's home race then turned into a nightmare as Acosta also overtook Martin, knocking him off the podium positions, before Aldeguer also got past. Once Marc reclaimed the lead, there was no stopping him, despite Alex's relentless pursuit. "With Marc, it's true that it was really difficult to attack him because the last sector from him was unbelievable," Alex said. As the Ducati rider took the chequered flag ahead of his brother, a stone-faced Bezzecchi watched on from the Aprilia garage as he fell 33 points behind the leading pair having led the championship earlier this season. Raul Fernandez, Fabio Di Giannantonio, Enea Bastianini, Luca Marini and Fabio Quartararo completed the top 10.

item.title: With eye on bigger picture, Dodgers chase series win vs. Marlins
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are a determined bunch.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Los Angeles Dodgers are a determined bunch. On Sunday afternoon, the Dodgers (90-58) will try to win their three-game series over the host Miami Marlins (73-76). But their real goal goes much further as they are trying to get everyone healthy so they can make their strongest possible push toward a third straight World Series title. It's a feat no team has accomplished since the 1998-2000 New York Yankees. There are few flaws with the Dodgers, whose primary concern is that this is an older team with nine hitters age 31 or older. That list includes starters such as Freddie Freeman, 37; Max Muncy, 36; Teoscar Hernandez, 33; and Mookie Betts, who turns 34 next month. On the pitching side, closer Edwin Diaz is 32 and has produced just 13 2/3 innings and an 11.85 ERA this season due to injuries. In addition, Blake Snell has made just seven starts; and fellow 33-year-old Tyler Glasnow has made 11 starts, including a 4-3 loss to the Marlins on Saturday. Given that age/injury vulnerability, the Dodgers are working in younger players such as 21-year-old DH Josue De Paula, who made his MLB debut on Friday. A New York City native, De Paula had spent this entire season at Double-A, hitting .303 with 37 doubles, 27 homers, 104 RBIs, 31 steals in 41 tries and a .948 OPS. Despite his youth, De Paula's poise has impressed Dodgers manager Dave Roberts. "He has that (catcher) Will Smith heartbeat," Roberts told MLB.com. "His demeanor is very calm." Los Angeles will turn to right-hander Emmet Sheehan (5-8, 5.08 ERA) on Sunday. Sheehan recorded his first win since June 28 after allowing one run on three hits in 5 2/3 innings of a 6-3 victory over the Cincinnati Reds on Monday. He has yet to face Miami in his career. Meanwhile, the Marlins present a contrast to the Dodgers. While the Dodgers have the highest payroll in the majors at approximately $378 million, per Spotrac, the Marlins are next-to-last at just over $82 million. While the Dodgers will make the playoffs this year for the 14th consecutive season, the Marlins have played postseason ball just four times in their entire history. The best thing that can be said about the Marlins is that they will battle. A case in point came this past Wednesday when they fell behind by eight runs to the Mets; battled back to tie the score at 8-8; fell behind 14-8; battled back again ... only to lose 15-14. On Sunday, the Marlins will start right-hander Eury Perez (7-11. 3.94). Perez may be tiring. At age 23, the third-year major-leaguer has set career highs in starts (26) and innings (139.1). After posting a 1.80 ERA in June and a 1.69 ERA in July, Perez had a 3.46 ERA in August. In two starts in September, he has an ERA of 11.42. He has only one career appearance against the Dodgers, pitching six scoreless innings but coming away with no-decision. As for Miami's ability to punch above its weight, nobody encapsulates that better than Javier Sanoja, who won the National League utility player Gold Glove in 2025. Although undersized at a listed 5-7 and 150 pounds, Sanoja posted a .930 OPS from August 1 through Friday's series opener. That's in contrast to his .536 OPS as a rookie and his .683 OPS last year. "My (plate) discipline is helping me the most," Sanoja told MLB.com. "I want to do more so that they continue putting me in the lineup." --Field Level Media

item.title: Jays, Orioles in thick of AL wild-card race as games dwindle
item.description: The Toronto Blue Jays will count on ace Dylan Cease on Sunday afternoon in the rubber match of their crucial three-game series with the visiting Baltimore Orioles.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Toronto Blue Jays will count on ace Dylan Cease on Sunday afternoon in the rubber match of their crucial three-game series with the visiting Baltimore Orioles. The Blue Jays won 7-3 on Saturday after losing 7-4 on Friday. Toronto (74-75) has a 5-4 lead in the season series with Baltimore (72-77), with head-to-head records being the first tiebreaker for teams trying to reach the playoffs. With the Cleveland Guardians losing 4-3 on Saturday to the Minnesota Twins, the Blue Jays are one game out of the third American League wild-card berth, and Baltimore is two games behind Toronto. The two teams will meet again for three games in Baltimore in the final week of the season. The Blue Jays had considered taking advantage of their off day on Thursday to pitch Cease (10-5, 2.40 ERA) on Saturday. But considering the right-hander's workload and dip in velocity on Monday in a no-decision on the road against the Athletics, it was decided to start him on Sunday. "I think it's just late in the season," Cease said. "I've got to kind of roll with what I've got and figure out how I can maybe maximize it a little better." Cease allowed five runs (four earned) in five innings to the A's in West Sacramento, Calif., on Monday. The Athletics stole five bases with Cease on the mound and went on to win 6-5 in walk-off fashion. "I wish I had a little more focus on that," Cease said of the stolen bases. "I kind of just let it happen. They definitely took advantage." Cease is 3-1 with a 3.89 ERA in seven career starts against the Orioles. Baltimore is expected to counter with left-hander Trevor Rogers (10-9, 4.15 ERA), who is 0-1 with a 3.86 ERA in four career starts against Toronto. Starting with two innings from opener Spencer Miles, the Blue Jays used seven pitchers on Saturday. Because of a poor three-inning start from Kyle Bradish, who allowed five runs, Baltimore used five pitchers. "I mean, terrible," said Bradish, who is 0-5 in nine starts since his last win on July 22. "Giving up way too much damage, walking guys. Just putting our team in a big hole to start the game more times than not." The Orioles are in a more precarious position than the Blue Jays with 13 games to play. "If we want to be in the playoffs, we're playing playoff games right now," Orioles catcher Carlos Narvaez said. "The mentality has to be to win every game. That's why it's very frustrating for everybody here -- but from my end, too. Like, we needed this game. We cannot go back now. We got 13 left. It's on us. It's in our hands. It's frustrating, man." Orioles manager Craig Albernaz said his team will have no difficulty re-focusing after the loss on Saturday. "Our guys are not going to dwell on it, turn the page fast, because tomorrow's a day game, and Dylan Cease is on the mound, which is not an easy task," Albernaz said. "But our guys are ready for it. But yeah, we can't dwell on it, and they won't dwell on it. We've got to turn the page fast." Baltimore's Pete Alonso hit his 35th home run of the season, and 299th of his career, on Saturday. He also is one RBI short of hitting the 100 mark for the fifth time in his career. Toronto got homers from Alejandro Kirk and Brett Bateman, who also hit his first career major league homer in the ninth inning Friday. Rudy Martin Jr., 30, who made his major league debut as a pinch runner on Friday for Toronto, started in left field Saturday and was 0-for-2 with a walk. He made his first appearance in the minors in 2015 after the Kansas City Royals selected him in the 25th round of the 2014 MLB Draft. --Field Level Media

item.title: Xi impulsa lazos económicos del "Gran BRICS" para dar al bloque un mayor rol a nivel global
item.description: El presidente chino, Xi Jinping, dio a conocer el domingo una serie de iniciativas en ámbitos que van desde la inteligencia artificial hasta el comercio, con el fin de profundizar la cooperación entre las economías emergentes del "Gran BRICS", en un momento en que Pekín busca convertir al grupo en una plataforma práctica para el desarrollo del Sur Global.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El presidente chino, Xi Jinping, dio a conocer el domingo una serie de iniciativas en ámbitos que van desde la inteligencia artificial hasta el comercio, con el fin de profundizar la cooperación entre las economías emergentes del "Gran BRICS", en un momento en que Pekín busca convertir al grupo en una plataforma práctica para el desarrollo del Sur Global. La cooperación en ámbitos que van desde la política y la seguridad hasta la economía y las finanzas constituye el principal eje de trabajo del grupo, y tanto la India, que ocupa la presidencia en 2026, como China, que lo hará en 2027, buscan una colaboración más amplia para potenciar su influencia a nivel mundial. El éxito de la "Iniciativa del Gran BRICS" depende de que se sienten unas bases sólidas para una cooperación pragmática, dijo Xi en la cumbre anual de líderes celebrada en Nueva Delhi, informó la agencia oficial de noticias Xinhua. Los países del "Gran BRICS" deberían cooperar aún más, mantener la estabilidad de las cadenas industriales y de suministro, y fomentar un mercado integrado, señaló Xi en la sesión de clausura de la cumbre. China tomará la iniciativa en la creación de una "Zona de Código Abierto de IA de los BRICS" para promover la cooperación en materia de grandes modelos lingüísticos, formación en IA y un ecosistema abierto de IA, añadió Xi. Asimismo, propuso una asociación para crear una Zona Económica Especial de los BRICS y dijo que China acogerá el próximo año un Foro de Comercio de Servicios de los BRICS para impulsar los vínculos comerciales y de inversión. AMPLIACIÓN DEL PAPEL DEL GRUPO DEL "GRAN BRICS" El BRICS se ha ampliado para incluir a Irán, Indonesia, Egipto, Etiopía y los Emiratos Árabes Unidos, más allá de la composición original de hace dos décadas —formada por Brasil, Rusia, India, China y Sudáfrica—, cuyo objetivo era transformar un orden mundial dominado por Estados Unidos. Además, los diez países socios abarcan economías emergentes de Asia, África, América Latina y Oriente Medio, ampliando así su alcance por todo el Sur Global. China y Rusia se refieren en ocasiones a este bloque más amplio como el "Gran BRICS". BRICS AYUDA A CREAR UN ORDEN MUNDIAL MÁS JUSTO, DICE PUTIN Los beneficios de las soluciones desarrolladas en el seno del BRICS no deberían limitarse únicamente al BRICS, sino que deberían adaptarse y hacerse accesibles para satisfacer las necesidades del Sur Global, dijo anteriormente el primer ministro indio, Narendra Modi, en unas declaraciones. El presidente ruso, Vladímir Putin, calificó al BRICS de poderosa fuerza impulsora para la creación de un nuevo orden mundial más justo y multipolar, e instó a sus miembros a encontrar formas de combinar las ventajas competitivas de sus respectivas economías. La cumbre se celebra en medio de la reanudación de los combates en la región del Golfo, con ataques recíprocos entre Estados Unidos e Irán, y con los hutíes —respaldados por Irán— ampliando el conflicto mediante el lanzamiento de ataques contra Arabia Saudita. Sin embargo, la cumbre del fin de semana logró un importante éxito diplomático el sábado, al alcanzar un consenso sobre una declaración conjunta respaldada por Irán y los Emiratos Árabes Unidos. En términos generales, la declaración expresaba una profunda preocupación por la continua escalada de tensión en Oriente Medio e instaba a actuar con la máxima moderación. Por otra parte, el presidente iraní, Masoud Pezeshkian, también se reunió con el príncipe heredero de Abu Dabi al margen de la cumbre, en lo que supuso el encuentro de más alto nivel entre funcionarios de ambos países desde el inicio del conflicto. Abordaron temas que abarcaban desde la distensión y la estabilidad hasta los esfuerzos para promover la paz y el desarrollo regionales.

item.title: Easy win for South Africa as they sweep ODI series
item.description: South Africa swept their three-match One Day International series against neighbours Namibia with a comprehensive nine-wicket win in Sunday’s last clash.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Africa swept their three-match One Day International series against neighbours Namibia with a comprehensive nine-wicket win in Sunday’s last clash. South Africa captain Bjorn Fortuin returned to the team, after being rested on Friday, to take 4-33 as Namibia, who elected to bat first, were dismissed for 156 runs in the 37th over. In reply, openers Connor Esterhuizen and Jordan Hermann put on 150 for the first wicket before Hermann was bowled for 77, seven runs short of the victory. Esterhuizen finished unbeaten on 68 while new batsman Dewald Brevis hit a six to win the game with 28.3 overs to spare. Both Esterhuizen and Hermann had scored centuries in the first two ODIs against Namibia and kept up their form for an easy triumph. South Africa, who rested almost all of their limited-overs regulars, were also comfortable winners in the first two ODIs of the first series between the neighbours, who along with Zimbabwe will co-host next year’s World Cup.

item.title: La Turquie arrête 26 personnes lors de raids visant la communauté LGBTQ+
item.description: Les autorités turques ont interpellé 26 personnes et perquisitionné les locaux de six associations LGBTQ+ lors d'une série de descentes menées à la suite d'allégations de prostitution et d'obscénité, ont indiqué les procureurs.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Les autorités turques ont interpellé 26 personnes et perquisitionné les locaux de six associations LGBTQ+ lors d'une série de descentes menées à la suite d'allégations de prostitution et d'obscénité, ont indiqué les procureurs. Cette répression s'inscrit dans le cadre d'une campagne qui, selon le gouvernement, vise à protéger les valeurs familiales. Le bureau du procureur général d'Istanbul a indiqué que des opérations avaient été menées dans 12 provinces contre 38 suspects au cours du week-end, au cours desquelles les autorités ont saisi de la drogue, du matériel numérique, de l'alcool de contrebande et une arme à feu. L'association LGBTQ+ Kaos GL, basée à Ankara, a déclaré qu'au moins 50 activistes avaient été placés en garde à vue – un chiffre supérieur à celui avancé par le bureau du procureur général –, dont plus de 10 ont été interpellés lors de perquisitions policières à leur domicile. Elle a par ailleurs indiqué que les autorités avaient bloqué l'accès à des dizaines de sites internet et de comptes sur les réseaux sociaux liés à des organisations LGBTI+, à des militants et à des défenseurs des droits. Nommée "Ma famille est en sécurité", cette campagne de répression menée par le gouvernement intervient alors que le président Recep Tayyip Erdogan promeut une "décennie de la famille et de la population" censée lutter contre la baisse du taux de natalité et le vieillissement démographique. Les organisations de défense des droits de l'homme accusent le gouvernement turc de s'en prendre de plus en plus à la communauté LGBTQ+ depuis quelques années par le biais d'un durcissement du discours et des restrictions. "Le véritable nom de cette opération n'est pas 'Ma famille est en sécurité' ; il s'agit de discrimination d'État, d'une politique de la peur et du démantèlement de la société civile", a déclaré l'Association turque des droits de l'homme sur X. Le parquet a fait état de preuves montrant que des enfants et des mineurs subissent une influence inappropriée en matière d'orientation sexuelle et d'identité de genre. Le ministre de la Justice, Akin Gurlek, a déclaré que les enquêtes coordonnées par les parquets d'Istanbul, d'Ankara, d'Izmir, d'Aydin et de Mersin donnaient lieu à des poursuites judiciaires à l'encontre de 162 suspects, neuf associations et 13 entreprises réparties dans 15 provinces.

item.title: Grayson Rodriguez, Angels out to salvage finale vs. Nationals
item.description: The Washington Nationals will go for their first series sweep in over a month when they host the Los Angeles Angels on Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Washington Nationals will go for their first series sweep in over a month when they host the Los Angeles Angels on Sunday afternoon. Washington (69-81) prevailed 6-5 in 10 innings on Saturday, winning its second straight game after losing seven in a row. The Angels (56-92) have lost two straight after taking two of three games from the Boston Red Sox. Los Angeles will try to salvage the finale behind Grayson Rodriguez (4-7, 6.28 ERA), who will oppose fellow right-hander Jake Irvin (2-9, 5.52) on Sunday. After a strong August that saw him lower his ERA by nearly two runs, Rodriguez has struggled to begin September. He is 0-2 with an 8.10 ERA in two starts, allowing nine runs on 13 hits -- including four homers -- in 10 innings. Last time out, Rodriguez gave up five runs on six hits in four innings of a 5-2 loss to the Red Sox on Monday. One of the homers was a three-run shot by his former teammate with the Baltimore Orioles, Adley Rutschman. "In that moment, that fastball, that's the best pitch to me," Rodriguez said. "It probably could have been up and away, up and in, but he's a good hitter, man. Caught me for a long time. Kind of weird seeing him in the box in a different uniform. But to me, heater's the best pitch. So there's no regrets." Rodriguez won his only prior start against Washington, allowing one run over 5 2/3 innings in 2023. Since returning from the injured list in late July, Irvin is 0-5 with a 5.90 ERA. Last time out he gave up three early runs on eight hits in 5 2/3 innings in a 3-2 loss to the San Diego Padres on Monday. "Hopefully he's taking the positives from this one, just the ability he had after the third inning to shut them down the rest of the way and keep us in the game was huge," Nationals manager Blake Butera said. Irvin has yet to face the Angels in his career. Saturday's game featured a wild final three innings. Trailing 4-0, the Angels scored three runs in the eighth and two in the ninth as the Nationals' bullpen added to its MLB record by posting its 39th blown save of the season. However, the Nationals tied the score in the ninth off Los Angeles closer Ben Joyce and won in the 10th when automatic runner CJ Abrams led a double steal and then scored from third on a misplayed grounder. James Wood stole his 20th base of the season, making him and Abrams just the 11th pair of teammates in MLB history to hit 30 homers and steal 20 bases in the same season. "The athleticism -- they're both dynamic players and bring so much to the table outside of when they're in the batter's box," Butera said. "They're both total-package players, and I'm lucky just to be able to sit there and watch them do their thing." Vaughn Grissom homered in the eighth inning for the Angels, who fell to 4-14 in extra-inning games. "Everybody wants to win, but we've got to go back and try to see how we can improve in those areas and get us more opportunities, I guess, to win those," manager Kurt Suzuki said. --Field Level Media

item.title: Pétrole-L'arrêt de l'oléoduc saoudien attaqué menace 4% de l'approvisionnement mondial
item.description: L'Arabie saoudite va épuiser ses stocks de pétrole destinés à l'exportation si elle ne remet pas en service son principal oléoduc vers la mer Rouge d'ici quelques jours, ce qui entraînerait une perte pouvant atteindre 4% de l'approvisionnement mondial, selon des acheteurs de brut saoudiens et des traders.
item.dc:creator: Alex Lawler, Dmitry Zhdannikov
item.content:encoded: L'Arabie saoudite va épuiser ses stocks de pétrole destinés à l'exportation si elle ne remet pas en service son principal oléoduc vers la mer Rouge d'ici quelques jours, ce qui entraînerait une perte pouvant atteindre 4% de l'approvisionnement mondial, selon des acheteurs de brut saoudiens et des traders. Une nouvelle baisse des flux saoudiens aggraverait le choc d'offre de pétrole, qui a déjà poussé les prix des carburants à des niveaux records, alimenté l'inflation à travers le monde et propulsé les rendements obligataires américains à leurs plus hauts niveaux depuis la crise financière de 2008. Depuis que des attaques de drones ont contraint l'Arabie saoudite à fermer vendredi son important oléoduc est-ouest, Ryad n'a pas communiqué de façon précise sur l'ampleur des dégâts ni sur la durée de la mise hors service de l'infrastructure. Des sources interrogées par Reuters ont fourni des estimations divergentes : l'une d'entre elles a indiqué que les réparations pourraient prendre jusqu'à cinq à six semaines, tandis qu'une autre a estimé que le problème pourrait être résolu plus rapidement et que le pompage pourrait reprendre partiellement pendant la durée des travaux. Le service de presse du gouvernement saoudien et le ministère de l'Énergie n'ont pas répondu dans l'immédiat à des demandes de commentaires. Au cours des six derniers mois, l'oléoduc traversant le désert de la péninsule arabique a épargné à l'Arabie saoudite l'essentiel de l'impact de la fermeture du détroit d'Ormuz, résultant de la guerre entre les Etats-Unis et l'Iran, qui a paralysé les exportations de ses voisins. Le plus grand exportateur mondial a utilisé cet oléoduc pour acheminer environ 4 millions de barils par jour - soit environ 4% de l'approvisionnement mondial - vers le port de Yanbu, sur la mer Rouge. Cependant, avec la mise hors service de l'oléoduc, Yanbu ne dispose plus désormais que de stocks lui permettant de maintenir ses exportations pendant cinq à sept jours seulement, selon trois sources du secteur ayant une bonne connaissance des exportations saoudiennes. L'Arabie saoudite dispose également de stocks suffisants pour approvisionner ses clients pendant plusieurs jours à partir des ports égyptiens d'Ain Soukhna, sur la mer Rouge, et de Sidi Kerir, sur la Méditerranée, a indiqué une quatrième source. La capacité de stockage de Yanbu s'élève à environ 35 millions de barils, selon les estimations du secteur, tandis qu'Ain Soukhna et Sidi Kerir peuvent stocker respectivement 18 millions et 20 millions de barils. Ces stocks ne sont pas pleins et finiront par s'épuiser si l'oléoduc est-ouest ne reprend pas ses activités, ont déclaré les quatre sources. L'approvisionnement en pétrole saoudien a déjà atteint en août son plus bas niveau depuis plus de trois décennies en raison de la réduction des flux via le détroit d'Ormuz et la mer Rouge, a déclaré vendredi l'Agence internationale de l'énergie (AIE). L'approvisionnement mondial en pétrole baissera cette année de 5,7 millions de barils par jour, soit environ 6%, selon les estimations de l'AIE, qui coordonne les politiques énergétiques occidentales. Outre l'attaque contre l'oléoduc, les combattants houthis au Yémen, qui ont menacé les livraisons de pétrole saoudien, se sont emparés vendredi d'une île située à l'embouchure de la mer Rouge. Le Moyen-Orient fournissait environ 22 millions de barils de pétrole par jour avant la guerre. Les flux transitant par le détroit d'Ormuz ont ralenti pour atteindre seulement 6 à 9 millions de barils par jour, selon des sources du secteur. L'Arabie saoudite a indiqué à l'Opep la semaine dernière que sa production pétrolière était tombée à seulement 6,2 millions de barils par jour en août contre 10,9 millions de barils par jour en février, avant le début de la guerre.

item.title: Cam Schlittler, Yanks continue playoff push in clash against Mets
item.description: Starting pitcher Gerrit Cole described the New York Yankees playing games in September as the postseason approaches as "the fun part" while Francisco Lindor lamented how the New York Mets did not do enough early this season to put themselves in contention for the playoffs.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Starting pitcher Gerrit Cole described the New York Yankees playing games in September as the postseason approaches as "the fun part" while Francisco Lindor lamented how the New York Mets did not do enough early this season to put themselves in contention for the playoffs. On Saturday, the Yankees' quest to clinch a postseason spot was partially derailed by the Mets continuing their late hot streak after falling out of contention earlier in the season. After a rough performance Saturday and with American League Cy Young Award favorite Cam Schlittler on the mound Sunday afternoon, the Yankees will attempt to move toward securing their ninth playoff appearance in 10 seasons when they host the Mets in the season finale of the Subway Series. The Yankees (85-63) are 17-8 in their past 25 games despite allowing six homers in Saturday's 12-2 loss to the Mets. Cole allowed three homers in 4 1/3 innings before the Yankees took one of their worst defeats this season. "This is the fun part of it, because the reward is close," he said. "Getting to the postseason, being able to chase your ultimate goal -- these are the games you look forward to the most." With 14 games left, the Yankees begin Sunday needing a win, and then a loss by the Toronto Blue Jays, to join the Los Angeles Dodgers as the only teams to make the playoffs in nine of the past 10 seasons since 2017. The Mets (69-79), meanwhile, are trying to fend off clinching a losing season for as long as possible after falling 19 games under .500 in July, losing 12 straight in April, and trading several players at the Aug. 3 trade deadline. Since the trades, the Mets are 22-13 and are coming off setting a Subway Series record with six homers on Saturday. The team also is 5-1 in its past six games, collecting 51 runs, 17 homers and batting .279. Lindor, who missed two months of the season with a calf injury and is hitting .234, is coming off a big showing with a leadoff homer off Cole and a grand slam in the eighth. Lindor has four of his five multi-homer games since Aug. 30 and heads into his first encounter against Schlittler batting .314 in 26 Subway Series games since joining the Mets in 2021. "This is what we should have been doing from the beginning, but it's part of the journey and part of the year and try to make the most of it," Lindor said. Said Mets interim manager Andy Green: "We didn't meet expectations for the vast majority of the season, but where this group is mentally right now, when we step on the field, we expect to win. We don't really care who's on the other side." Schlittler (13-6, 2.01 ERA), who leads the majors by allowing one earned run or less in 20 starts, will face the Mets for the second time in his career. He has allowed one run or less in his past six starts since Aug. 3 and has 49 strikeouts in those games. Schlittler last pitched on Tuesday, when he allowed one run on three hits and struck out 10 in a 5-3 win over the Colorado Rockies. In his only appearance against the Mets, on May 15 at Citi Field, he allowed one run on two hits in 6 2/3 innings and earned the victory when he also struck out nine while Lindor was on the injured list. The Yankees won 5-2. After getting seven impressive innings Saturday from Zac Thornton (two runs over seven innings), the Mets will start their third rookie of the series when right-hander Christian Scott (4-4, 3.81 ERA) faces the Yankees for the first time. Scott most recently pitched in last Sunday's 4-2 win over the San Francisco Giants, when he allowed two runs on four hits in 4 2/3 innings before the Mets scored four times in the eighth inning. --Field Level Media

item.title: Carney défend l'idée de faire du Canada un "membre associé" de l'UE-presse
item.description: Le Premier ministre canadien Mark Carney souhaite resserrer les liens l'Union européenne (UE) et examine la possibilité pour son pays de devenir un "membre associé" du bloc, rapporte dimanche le Wall Street Journal.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le Premier ministre canadien Mark Carney souhaite resserrer les liens l'Union européenne (UE) et examine la possibilité pour son pays de devenir un "membre associé" du bloc, rapporte dimanche le Wall Street Journal. L'UE, qui ne s'est pas montrée très souple par le passé en matière de règles d'adhésion, serait ouverte à l'idée d'accorder au Canada un statut de membre associé qui reste à créer, ajoute le journal, citant des responsables anonymes, tant du côté de l'UE que du Canada. L'ambassade du Canada à Bruxelles et les porte-parole de la Commission européenne n'ont pas répondu à des demandes de commentaires. L'escalade dans la guerre commerciale entre le Canada et les États-Unis a rendu plus urgente encore pour Ottawa la recherche d'autres partenaires. Les relations entre les deux pays se sont nettement dégradées depuis le retour du président Donald Trump à la Maison blanche, début 2025, en raison de désaccords sur le commerce et d'autres sujets. Leur différend commercial a conduit à la mise en place de droits de douane portant sur des dizaines de milliards de dollars d'échanges transfrontaliers. Le Canada et l'UE discutent actuellement des moyens de permettre la libre circulation des biens, des services et des travailleurs canadiens impliqués dans des chaînes d'approvisionnement stratégiques telles que l'énergie, l'intelligence artificielle, la défense et les minéraux critiques, ce qui reviendrait à déplacer de fait la frontière de l'UE, selon le Wall Street Journal. Le Canada et l'UE discutent également de la pose de câbles sous-marins, de la construction conjointe de centres de données, de solutions de stockage dans le cloud ainsi que de nouveaux réseaux satellitaires et d'infrastructures permettant d'acheminer l'énergie canadienne vers l'UE, précise le journal. Mark Carney s'est entretenu régulièrement avec plusieurs dirigeants de l'UE, notamment le président français Emmanuel Macron, au sujet de la possibilité de permettre aux Canadiens de vivre et de travailler sans visa dans l'UE, toujours selon le Wall Street Journal, qui cite deux sources anonymes au fait du dossier. Les deux dirigeants se rencontreront le 20 septembre à Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon à l'occasion d'un déplacement d'Emmanuel Macron dans l'archipel. "Dans un monde marqué par le retour des rapports de force, les tensions géopolitiques et de nouvelles dépendances, la France et le Canada partagent une même ambition : travailler ensemble, et avec tous les pays qui partagent ces valeurs, renforcer leur capacité à décider, et à agir par eux-mêmes", a déclaré l'Elysée. Le projet visant à resserrer les liens entre le Canada et l'UE n'est toutefois pas une mince affaire, comme l'a montré la vive opposition suscitée par un accord commercial pourtant plus modeste noué entre les deux parties. Plus d'une décennie après la conclusion de celui-ci et neuf ans après son entrée en vigueur à titre provisoire, plusieurs pays de l'UE ne l'ont ainsi toujours pas ratifié.

item.title: Saudi pipeline outage threatens loss of 4% of global oil supply
item.description: Saudi Arabia will run out of oil stocks for exports if it doesn't restart its major pipeline to the Red Sea within days, leading to a loss of up to 4% of global supply, Saudi oil buyers and traders said. A further decline in Saudi flows will worsen the global supply crunch, which has already pushed global fuel prices to record highs, spurred inflation around the world and sent U.S. bond yields to the highest levels since the 2008 financial crisis.
item.dc:creator: Alex Lawler, Dmitry Zhdannikov
item.content:encoded: Saudi Arabia will run out of oil stocks for exports if it doesn't restart its major pipeline to the Red Sea within days, leading to a loss of up to 4% of global supply, Saudi oil buyers and traders said. A further decline in Saudi flows will worsen the global supply crunch, which has already pushed global fuel prices to record highs, spurred inflation around the world and sent U.S. bond yields to the highest levels since the 2008 financial crisis. Since drone attacks forced Saudi Arabia to [USN:S8N44107L TEXT:"shut"] its huge east-west oil pipeline on Friday, Riyadh has not given full details about the extent of the damage or how long the route will stay off-line. Sources that spoke to Reuters gave varying estimates, with one saying the damage could take as long as five to six weeks to repair, while another said it could be fixed sooner and could resume pumping partially while repairs are ongoing. Saudi Arabia's government media office and energy ministry did not immediately respond to requests for comment. For the past six months, the pipeline running through the desert across the Arabian Peninsula has spared Saudi Arabia from the brunt of the impact of the wartime shutdown of the Strait of Hormuz that has crippled exports from its neighbours. The world's biggest exporter has used the pipeline to reroute around 4 million barrels per day — around 4% of global supply — to the port of Yanbu on the Red Sea. But with the pipeline out of service, Yanbu now has stocks to maintain exports for just five to seven days, according to three industry sources familiar with Saudi exports. Saudi Arabia also has stocks to supply customers for several days from Egypt's ports of Ain Sukhna on the Red Sea and Sidi Kerir on the Mediterranean, a fourth source said. Yanbu storage capacity stands at around 35 million barrels, according to industry estimates, with Ain Sukhna and Sidi Kerir able to store 18 million and 20 million barrels respectively. Stocks are not full and will ultimately run out without the east-west pipeline resuming operations, the four sources said. Saudi oil supply has already fallen to a more than [USN:L6N4530LR TEXT:"three-decade low"] in August on reduced flows via Hormuz and the Red Sea, the International Energy Agency said on Friday. World oil supply will [USN:L6N4530I5 TEXT:"decline"] this year by 5.7 million bpd, or about 6%, the IEA, which coordinates Western energy policies, said. In addition to the attack on the pipeline, Houthi fighters in Yemen who have threatened Saudi oil shipments seized an island on Friday in the mouth of the Red Sea . The Middle East supplied around 22 million barrels per day of oil before the war. Flows through the Strait of Hormuz have slowed to just 6 million to 9 million bpd, industry sources say. Saudi Arabia told OPEC last week that its oil production had dropped to just 6.2 million bpd in August from 10.9 million bpd in February before the start of the war.

item.title: New era beckons for holders Al-Ahli ahead of Asian Champions League title defence
item.description: Al-Ahli launch the defence of the Asian Champions League Elite title against Pakhtakor on Monday under new management and with a new-look squad as the Saudi Pro League side attempt to become the first club to win the trophy three times in a row.
item.dc:creator: Michael Church
item.content:encoded: Al-Ahli launch the defence of the Asian Champions League Elite title against Pakhtakor on Monday under new management and with a new-look squad as the Saudi Pro League side attempt to become the first club to win the trophy three times in a row. Matthias Jaissle, who led the Jeddah-based outfit to back-to-back successes, departed in August to join Newcastle United in the Premier League and left behind a squad in the throes of an overhaul. Riyad Mahrez, the former Manchester City winger who had been instrumental in both of Al-Ahli's title triumphs, left the club at the expiration of his contract in June while midfielder Franck Kessie joined Atalanta in Serie A. Their departures followed the exit of Roberto Firmino last year as Al-Ahli have refreshed their squad in an effort to remain competitive both at home and in continental competition. Former FC Twente and Shakhtar Donetsk coach Marino Pusic has replaced Jaissle at the helm with Al-Ahli one of five Saudi Pro League clubs competing in the newly expanded league phase of the competition. Sixteen clubs – up from 12 in the two previous seasons – will feature on each side of the continent, with Al-Ahli joined by four-times champions Al-Hilal, Saudi title holders Al-Nassr plus Al-Ittihad and Al-Qadsiah to complete the country's quota. Clubs will play eight matches in the league phase with the first eight finishers from west and east Asia advancing to the last 16, with the first round of knockout matches played on a regional basis. The quarter-finals, semi-finals and final will all be hosted on a centralised basis in Saudi Arabia for the third season in a row from April 23 with the decider to be held on May 1. Al-Ahli won the title last season with victory in Jeddah over Japan's Machida Zelvia and, like their Saudi Pro League counterparts, the J-League will be represented by a record five clubs due to the expansion. Machida, however, will not be among the participants after finishing outside the qualifying positions last season. The Japanese will be represented by domestic champions Kashima Antlers, who won the Asian title in 2018, plus former winners Gamba Osaka, Kyoto Sanga, Kashiwa Reysol and Vissel Kobe. Kashima begin their campaign hosting Australia's Newcastle Jets while three-times winners Pohang Steelers will seek to turn around a poor run of form in the competition by South Korean clubs when they face Beijing Guoan.

item.title: Payton Tolle, Red Sox strive for strong showing vs. Royals
item.description: Impressive left-handers will be on display as the Boston Red Sox and visiting Kansas City Royals play a decisive contest of their three-game weekend series on Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
